Learned today, not yet rules elsewhere: (a) a lane that moves or renames something many tests walk, or adds a page, a route or a table, runs the WHOLE browser chain in its folder in chunks of six files before its last push (each file directly with `--no-build` after one building run): GitHub's check takes thirty minutes and stops at the first failing file, and 2.168 lost three trips; (b) the landing script runs only the tests it is given: after two lanes land that touch the same sentence or list, run the unit tests of both in the main folder (the build branch was red for an hour on the login check's new words); (c) `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` pins the number of rows of the T4 table; (d) a pinned start-up sentence in `apps/web/src/server/container.test.ts` names the first table the owner login holds, in order: a lane that adds a table sorted before it corrects that word; (e) helpers overrun their limit of commands when a brief lists many items: give at most four items a session and say "count them"; (f) a helper's `git merge origin/build/stage-1` in its own lane is sometimes refused by the app's check: the brief must say the lead asks for it, or the lead merges; (g) publishing to an artifact needs one read of its page first, which costs 25 thousand tokens of the lead's conversation: let a Sonnet helper republish the first-look page.
